question.problem: Let $\mathcal{B}= \left\{ \mathbf{b}_1, \mathbf{b}_2 \right\}$ be a basis of $\mathbb{R}^2$ and ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14274943/assets/7138c7f0cf14978e4c345b91b7c5b5e38c4c74d00a83a5f9a0908249b5602045.svg) What are the coordinates of $\mathbf{x}$ relative to the basis $\mathcal{C}= \left\{ \mathbf{c}_1, \mathbf{c}_2 \right\},$ where $\mathbf{c}_1 = -\mathbf{b}_2$ and $\mathbf{c}_2 = -3\mathbf{b}_1?$
question.worked_solution:
Since ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14274943/assets/f2c4bc20db558b0e0498da6c9b8653f8e093a7b3a517a21ec07803cdf3debf98.svg) we can write $\mathbf{x}$ in terms of the vectors $\mathbf c_1$ and $\mathbf c_2,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =5{b}_{1}-2{b}_{2} \\  & =-2{b}_{2}+5{b}_{1} \\  & =2(-{b}_{2})-\frac{5}{3}(-3{b}_{1}) \\  & =2{c}_{1}-\frac{5}{3}{c}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14274943/assets/f6a8d41276d74ce726301f3cc83d87542d49115eb46cf0f836d20816cd660168.svg)
